Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.
It is submitted that Smt. Amod/mother-in-law of the deceased, Rajiv (devar) of the deceased and Bhole have been granted bail, para-13 of the affidavit has been placed for the same.
It is submitted that the applicant has no criminal history as stated in para- 14 of the affidavit.
It is submitted while placing para-12 of the affidavit that in the trial statement of four prosecution witnesses have been recorded.
It is submitted that looking to period of detention as he is in jail since 31.12.2020 he may be directed to be enlarged on bail.
6. Per contra, learned State counsel opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that the first bail application of the applicant has been rejected by this Court on merits vide order dated 10.7.2023.
It is submitted that four prosecution witnesses have been examined in the trial who have supported the prosecution version and as such the prosecution story remained intact.
It is submitted that trial is under progress in which four prosecution witnesses have been examined and as such release of the applicant at this stage may have adverse effect on the trial.
Therefore, the prayer for bail be rejected.

7. After having heard learned counsels for the parties and perusing the records, it is evident that the first bail application of the applicant has been rejected by this Court on merit vide order dated 10.7.2023 which reads as under:-
"1. List revised.
2.

Heard Ms. Neetu Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri J.P. Tripathi,
learned counsel for the State and perused the material on record.

3. This bail application under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed by the applicant Sanjeev, seeking enlargement on bail during trial in connection with Case Crime No. 1652 of 2020, under Sections 498-A, 323, 304-B, 504 IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act, registered at P.S. Civil Lines, District Moradabad.
4. The First Information Report of the present case has been lodged on 30.12.2020 by Smt. Raj Kumari alleging therein that her daughter aged about 19 years was married to the applicant.
There was demand of dowry by the applicant and three other accused persons named in the First Information Report.
They used to torture and harass her daughter.
Around two and half months, she made a complaint to the Mahila Thana about it.
Smt. Amod the mother-in-law of the deceased informed her that her daughter has consumed poison and died.
The First Information Report has thus been lodged.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant argued that although the applicant is the husband of the deceased but he has been falsely implicated in the present case.
It is argued that the deceased has not received any bodily injury.
The cause of death could not be ascertained hence viscera was preserved.

Learned counsel for the applicant while placing para 11 of the affidavit has argued that the deceased did not wanted to Sanjeev vs State Of U.P. on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178627377/
2 marry the applicant and her behaviour and activities were doubtful as she was having love affair with one Rajveer and when the applicant sought explanation from her she did not furnish any explanation of it.

It is argued that the deceased under the influence of the informant was causing pressure upon the applicant for living separately but the same was refused due to which she became annoyed and committed suicide.
He further argued that the applicant has no criminal history as stated in para 21 of the affidavit and is in jail since 31.12.2020.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the first informant and learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer for bail and argued that the applicant is the husband of the deceased.
She died in her matrimonial house after six months of marriage which is within seven years.

It is argued that there is burden upon the applicant, particularly,
he being husband of the deceased to discharge the same, however, up to this stage,
the applicant has failed to discharge the said burden.

It is argued that there is no reason for false implication of the applicant and as such the prayer for bail of the applicant be rejected.
7.
After having heard learned counsels for the parties and perusing the records, it is evident that the applicant is the husband of the deceased.
The deceased died after six months in her matrimonial house which is unnatural within seven years.
The applicant has failed to discharge the burden regarding the death of his wife in his house within six months of marriage.
I do not find it a fit case for bail.
8. Considering the totality of the case in particular, nature of evidence available on record, I am not inclined to release the applicant on bail.
9. The bail application is, accordingly, rejected."

8. The trial is under progress in which four prosecution witnesses have been examined and the statements of the said four prosecution witnesses which have been annexed as annexure nos. 5 and 6 to the affidavit, go to show that they have supported the prosecution case.

In so far as the bail granted to said three co-accused are concerned, the case of the applicant stands distinguishable with that of the said three co-accused since the applicant is the husband of the deceased.
The trial is under progress and release of the applicant at this stage may have adverse effect in the trial.
9. Looking into the facts and circumstances of the case as well as nature and gravity of the offence, I am not inclined to release the applicant on bail.
10. The bail application is, accordingly, rejected.
(Samit Gopal,J.) Order Date :- 5.2.2025/
